thread:
incident-bot: 🔥 [P1] east1 GPU pool saturated — autoscaler failing to provision; queue growth detected.
incident-bot: metrics: gpu_util=98%, pending_requests=12k, avg_queue_latency=4.2s, error_rate=4.6% (token gen failures).

maria (oncall): ack. pinging sre, ml-infra. I’m on it.
devin (sre-lead): I’m awake — looking at autoscaler logs now. Any customer-facing degradations?
ken (prod-support): Several customers reporting 503s in east1, some routed to degraded fallback but many still hitting primary. CS has a couple escalations.
lia (customer-success): Lia here — notified two enterprise customers (acme, fleetops). They see timeouts for long-form generation. Asking for ETA and mitigation steps.
priya (ml-infra): autoscaler scale-up requests are flapping: provisioning requests to east1-gpu-pool are returning "PendingAllocation" and then timing out. I see repeated AZ placement failures. looks like quota + gang-scheduling pressure.
devin (sre-lead): paste of recent autoscaler tail:
```
2026-03-15T10:02:12Z autoscaler: request_id=abc123 region=east1 desired=40 current=32 state=Provisioning
2026-03-15T10:04:08Z autoscaler: allocation_failed: reason=InsufficientHosts details={az:"east1-b", need:8} request=abc123
2026-03-15T10:05:50Z autoscaler: retrying allocation (attempt 3)
2026-03-15T10:06:40Z autoscaler: allocation_timeout request=abc123 -> rollback
```
devin (sre-lead): Also seeing kube-provisioner errors where pods stuck in ContainerCreating for >8m.
priya (ml-infra): KV caches are saturated for some pinned models; warmups are exacerbating memory pressure causing additional evicts and retries.
maria (oncall): Priorities: 1) stop queue growth and 2) reduce customer impact. Proposed quick mitigations?
devin (sre-lead): immediate steps I can do now: 1) enable cross-region spillover policy to force-fanout to west1 and eu1 for routing tier 0 (critical) and tier 1 (default). 2) Temporarily increase fallback weight to west1 in traffic router. 3) Drop non-critical background workloads (batch evals) from east1.
priya (ml-infra): I can patch model routing rules to prefer quantized variants in fallback regions to avoid heavy gpu types. That’ll reduce per-request footprint.
ken (prod-support): Can you annotate which customers still pinned to east1-only models? We need to call them if live routing change will affect latency/qual.
lia (customer-success): Acme is pinned to east1 but will accept fallback if we notify. Fleetops is strict — they need dedicated pool, I’ll page the account team.

maria (oncall): Devin — do the forced-fanout. Priya — start the routing patch. I’ll throttle ingress for low-priority API keys to buy time.

devin (sre-lead): executing: `rtrctl route update --region east1 --spillover-mode force-fanout --targets west1,eu1 --weight west1=0.7,eu1=0.3 --apply`
deploy-bot: starting deploy 7c9f... applying route-change to edge routers.
deploy-bot: ✅ route-change complete. propagation ~30s.
priya (ml-infra): pushing routing patch to prefer `quant_v2` variants in west1/eu1 for models tagged heavy. Command: `modelsctl override --region=west1,eu1 --prefer=quant_v2 --tag=heavy`
priya (ml-infra): done. will monitor for OOMs.

maria (oncall): throttling rule in place: low-priority keys now capped at 40rps across east1.
ken (prod-support): Noted drop in support tickets for smaller customers already. Enterprise tickets still active for Acme and Fleetops.

devin (sre-lead): autoscaler still failing to provision for east1 due to host shortage. As a fallback we can enable ephemeral burst capacity (reserved-spill) — that will temporarily borrow from dedicated burst pool with minor SLA hit. Need approval from infra-ops.
priya (ml-infra): ephemeral burst will help immediate capacity, but KV cache misses will spike as model pages cold-start. Expect transient latency increase for some flows.
lia (customer-success): I’ve messaged Acme — they accept fallbacks for now. Fleetops team is on call; they asked for a 2hr heads-up before any change to pinned routing.

maria (oncall): I’m paging infra-ops for burst pool. `@infra-ops please ack`
devin (sre-lead): while we wait, I’m increasing the node eviction threshold to allow smaller quantized instances to schedule: `k scale nodegroup east1-gpu --min=16 --max=64 --eviction-threshold=0.95` (incremental). Note: this risks OOM churn.

infra-ops (via deploy-bot): acknowledged. approving ephemeral burst lease id=burst-20260315-1 for 60m.
deploy-bot: provisioning burst pool nodes...
deploy-bot: burst nodes provisioned and joined cluster in ~90s.

devin (sre-lead): new nodes joined. autoscaler now able to schedule 10 more pods. queue length dropping from 12k -> 6.8k. avg_queue_latency -> 2.1s. error_rate -> 2.1%.
priya (ml-infra): KV cache warm jobs scheduled to prime the most-hit models on new nodes. Starting with top 20 keys.

ken (prod-support): Getting confirmations from Acme that requests are flowing (they see requests hitting west1). Fleetops still pinned — lia?
lia (customer-success): Fleetops agreed to emergency overlap routing for 30m while we stabilize. Will note potential quality diffs.

maria (oncall): Good. Recommended next steps: - keep burst lease for 60m - monitor autoscaler allocation (PRIOR) - start postmortem prep (assign SRE + ML infra) - notify status page + customers
devin (sre-lead): I’ll keep watch on allocation errors. Opening incident doc: `/incidents/2495001234` (working notes). Assigning postmortem: devin, priya, maria.
priya (ml-infra): root cause hypothesis: AZ-level host exhaustion + aggressive gang-scheduling for large GPU packs causing allocation timeouts; exacerbated by KV cache warmups and background evals. We'll run allocation trace after incident.

maria (oncall): Updating status page: "Degraded performance in east1 due to capacity provisioning issues; cross-region routing enabled; mitigation in progress."
ken (prod-support): I’ve posted templated customer updates and called two enterprise contacts.

incident-bot: 📌 Incident escalated to P1, channel pinned. Timeline logging started.

maria (oncall): will stay on this thread for the next hour; handing off to devin for overnight watch at 11:30Z. If anything spikes, page `#oncall` immediately.
devin (sre-lead): taking watch. will summarize final state before handoff.

deploy-bot: rollout: route-change reverted to normal weights at 2495001530 as demand normalized.

maria (oncall): last check: pending_requests=1.2k, avg_queue_latency=0.6s, error_rate=0.4%. dropping burst lease in 20m.

lia (customer-success): Acme and Fleetops logged as "affected - mitigated" in the incident tracker.

maria (oncall): closing active mitigation loop in 15m unless something changes. Postmortem owners: devin, priya, maria.

devin (sre-lead): noted. Will include allocation traces, autoscaler retries, and routing change timeline in postmortem.

maria (oncall): thanks team — good coordination. :thumbsup:
